name: Delaware veterans: Office of Veterans Services for claims help
organization: Delaware Department of State, Office of Veterans Services
description: Free help with VA claims, pension, survivor benefits and state veterans benefits from the Office of Veterans Services’ Veteran Service Officers. They work from the Dover headquarters and serve veterans in all three counties.
next_step: Call 302-739-2792 or email dcva.vso@delaware.gov to reach a Veteran Service Officer.
constraints: There is one service office for the state, in Dover; call before visiting.

name: Medicare counseling (Delaware Medicare Assistance Bureau, SHIP)
organization: Delaware Department of Insurance, Delaware Medicare Assistance Bureau (DMAB)
description: Free health insurance counseling for people with Medicare, including those under 65, from trained volunteers: Medicare, Medicaid, Medigap, Part D and long-term care insurance questions. DMAB is Delaware’s State Health Insurance Assistance Program.
next_step: Call 1-800-336-9500 or 302-674-7364 to set up a free counseling session at a site near you. For Medicare itself, call 800-MEDICARE (800-633-4227).
constraints: Counseling is by appointment. Have your Medicare card and drug list ready.

name: Delaware Long-Term Care Ombudsman and adult abuse reporting
organization: Delaware Health and Social Services: Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program; Division of Services for Aging and Adults with Physical Disabilities, Adult Protective Services
description: Advocacy for residents of nursing facilities, assisted living and board and care homes, and for people receiving home and community-based services. Adult Protective Services takes reports of abuse, neglect or exploitation of older adults and adults with disabilities.
next_step: Call the ombudsman hotline at 1-855-773-1002 (you can stay anonymous). To report abuse of an adult, call Adult Protective Services at 1-888-277-4302 (Delaware Relay: 711). For a nursing home or assisted living resident, you can also call the Division of Health Care Quality, 1-877-453-0012, 24/7. If someone is in immediate danger, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing agency.

name: Free legal help for older Delawareans
organization: Community Legal Aid Society, Inc. (CLASI), Elder Law Program
description: CLASI’s Elder Law Program gives free legal help to Delaware residents 60 and older, with no income test: powers of attorney, advance directives, fraud and financial exploitation, and consumer, housing and benefits problems. CLASI also serves people with low incomes and people with disabilities through its county offices.
next_step: If you are 60 or older, call the Elder Law Program at 302-575-0666. Or contact your county office: New Castle 302-575-0660 (Wilmington), Kent 302-674-8500 (Dover), Sussex 302-856-0038 (Georgetown); weekdays, by phone or in person.
constraints: The Elder Law Program does not do simple wills. CLASI does not take criminal or personal injury cases.

name: VA health care in Delaware
organization: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, VA Wilmington Healthcare System
description: Delaware veterans are served by the VA Wilmington Healthcare System: the Wilmington VA Medical Center (1601 Kirkwood Highway, Wilmington; 302-994-2511) and community clinics in Kent and Sussex counties. Vet Centers in Wilmington (302-994-1660) and Georgetown (302-225-9110) offer readjustment counseling.
next_step: For primary care appointments, call 800-461-8262 and select 2, or 302-994-2511. Not enrolled yet? Ask a Veteran Service Officer for help applying.
constraints: If a service you need is not offered near you, ask about travel benefits and community care.

name: Independent Resources, Inc.
description: A Center for Independent Living: disability-led help with daily living skills, peer support, advocacy, assistive technology referrals and moving from a nursing home back to the community. Any age and any disability; military service is not required.
next_step: Call with your county and goals. Ask about intake, home access, independent living skills or help leaving a facility.
constraints: A Center for Independent Living is a community support organization, not a residential care facility. Services depend on assessment and availability.
Wilmington office: Two Fox Point Centre, 6 Denny Road, Suite 101, Wilmington, DE 19809; accessible line 302-765-0194.
Dover office: 154 South Governors Avenue, Dover, DE 19904; 302-735-4599, accessible line 302-450-1699.
Milford office: 302-536-1387, accessible line 302-504-4754. The directory prints two street addresses for it (1609-A Middleford Road and 10 N Church Street, Milford, DE 19963); call before visiting.

next_step: Call SSVF intake with your county and housing situation: whether you are homeless now or at risk of losing housing, and who lives with you.
constraints: Serves only the areas listed; check that yours is included. Veteran-household, income and housing-status screening applies.
